title: Fomo Kernel Answer Provenance (issue #414, Wave A)
description: Mechanical provenance contract for a structured --agent-case submitted to consider. The preferred shape states one recommendation, non-empty support, and a counter_case only when material. Every claim remains distinguishably an engine computation, a sourced public fact, the user's own written record, or agent judgment. The legacy for/against shape stays readable so append-only evaluation history remains valid; new callers should use positiveCase.

recommendation.description: One explicit action judgment. Its provenance is agent_judgment; measured and public facts belong in support.

support.description: The facts and reasoning that make the recommendation useful.

counter_case.description: Optional. Include only an objection that could materially change the recommended action; an empty array is valid.

legacyCase.description: Read compatibility for evaluations recorded before the positive contract.

engineFactClaim.description: A claim that is, verbatim, the frozen engine result. Must mechanically resolve, and must quote every number exactly -- see answer_provenance.py's _resolve_anchor / _numeric_claim_matches.

claim.description: One sentence, the caller's own words.

anchor.description: Dot-separated path into the frozen {basis, consequence, rule_collisions} bundle an evaluation freezes (schemas/trade-evaluation.schema.json's own basis/consequence/rule_collisions properties). rule_collisions is addressed by rule_id, e.g. 'rule_collisions.rule-1.worsens', not by list position. Must resolve to exactly one scalar fact -- a path naming a container (an object or array) does not resolve.

rule_effect.description: Required, and must equal the frozen value exactly, when anchor targets a rule_collisions[...].rule_effect, .state or .worsens field whose frozen rule_effect is one of consequence.DIRECTIONAL_RULE_EFFECTS (#579). Forbidden on every other engine_fact claim. A six-way assertion where `worsens` below is a two-way one, and that is the point: the boolean cannot tell an improving trade from a stalled one, so a case that declared it correctly could still be built on the wrong transition -- which is what an owner-live walk saw when a sell reducing an over-cap position was described as breaking the rule. Free prose has no mechanical encoding of 'this trade improves it' a validator could check without scoring sentiment, so the direction rides beside the prose as structured metadata and is checked exactly, the same shape source/as_of already impose on a public_fact claim.

worsens.description: The pre-#579 direction. Required, and must equal the frozen value exactly, exactly when anchor targets a rule_collisions[...].state or .worsens field on a row recorded BEFORE rule_effect existed, whose frozen state is already_over and whose worsens is not null (both must hold; see consequence.py's own module docstring on why the two are independent axes). On a row that carries rule_effect it is optional -- the same fact said less precisely -- and still checked against the frozen value when supplied. Forbidden on every other engine_fact claim.

publicFactClaim.description: A claim sourced from outside both the engine and the user. source + as_of is the same provenance anchor condition-slot.schema.json's own observation $defs already cites this issue for, and the pair price-feed.schema.json already uses -- not source_ref/observed_at, a second name for the same idea this module deliberately avoids introducing.

source.description: The named external source, e.g. a filing, a press release, a recognized market-data provider.

as_of.description: The date the cited fact describes (or was read), an ISO date.

userRecordClaim.description: A claim quoted from the user's own written record (#844): a thesis, a falsifier, an open question, a prior decision or a stated stance they wrote themselves, read from the investing folder the skill is installed in. It is theirs -- never a public fact (no outside source stated it), never an engine fact (nothing computed it), never the agent's judgment (the agent did not form it). It carries the same source + as_of pair a public fact does, for the same reason: a record has a place it was read from and a date it carries. An AI-maintained status field about the user -- a health flag, a tier, a holding tag -- is not the user's belief and does not qualify.

claim.description: The user's own words, quoted, or one sentence reporting exactly what their note says.

source.description: The note it was read from, named the way the user would recognise it (a file path or a note title).

as_of.description: The date the note carries, or the day it was read when it carries none; an ISO date.

judgmentClaim.description: The agent's own reasoning, or a report of what the user said -- never presented as engine fact or public fact (issue #414: 'a user statement may only be described as what the user stated at that time; it is not promoted to an external fact').
